**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

Section 8 of the agreement already delivers the vendor-side protection this rule looks for, and it runs in our favour as licensee/host:

- **Vendor IP indemnity present and in our favour** — Commerce One must "indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers" against third-party claims that the Software infringes patent, copyright, trademark or trade secret rights. The indemnity expressly extends to our Customers, which is valuable given the hosting model.
- **Standard procedure** — prompt written notice, tender of control/defence/settlement to Commerce One at its expense, our cooperation at its expense, and a right for us to join the defence with our own counsel.
- **Remedies ladder** — procure the right, replace/modify to make non-infringing, or terminate and refund a pro-rated portion of fees paid (§8.1 / p0087).
- **Exclusions are narrow** — only use outside the Documentation and third-party modification with but-for causation (§8.2). This is tighter than the "usual exclusions" the fallback tolerates (no combination/specifications carve-out).
- **Better than fallback on the cap** — §9 carves Section 8 out of both the 12-month fees cap and the consequential-damages exclusion, so the indemnity is uncapped, exceeding the fallback's 3× annual fees super-cap.
- **No customer indemnity at all** — searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless" and "defend" returned hits only in §8.1, so there is no Corio-side indemnity to narrow.

Sub-elements short of the preferred position, noted in the rationale rather than redlined per the playbook's classification semantics: no separate heads for vendor breach of applicable law, vendor-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; and the refund is measured on fees "paid" rather than "paid or payable". Against an uncapped IP indemnity with no reciprocal obligation on us, these do not justify negotiating capital.
